pages.text:
$(l)Welcome to Chapter 2!$()

Here are several small spells you can use right away. Each is short and can be copied directly to test the effects while learning new runes.

pages.title: Light Spell
pages.text:
$(l)Rune Sequence:$()
$(9)$(l)Self VisionCoordinate MagicLight$()

$(l)Effect:$()Summons a magical light at eye position, illuminating surroundings. Especially useful when mining without placing torches.

$(l)Knowledge Points:$()
·$(9)VisionCoordinate$() and $(9)FootCoordinate$() are both query runes — one takes eye position, one takes foot position.
·$(9)MagicLight$() is a world-interaction rune that consumes mana — pops a coordinate from stack top and generates light there.

pages.title: Light Spell Related Rune Pages
pages.text: These are the runes used in this spell

pages.title: Ignite
pages.text:
$(l)Rune Sequence:$()
$(9)$(l)5.0 Ray Ignite$()

$(l)Effect:$()Ignites blocks within 5 blocks of your line of sight.

$(l)Knowledge Points:$()
·$(9)Ray$() pops distance from stack top, shoots a line from player's eyes, and pushes the hit block's coordinate onto the stack.
·$(9)Ignite$() pops coordinate and spawns fire above it.

Constants can be inserted directly into rune sequences

pages.title: Ignite Related Rune Pages
pages.text: These are the runes used in this spell

pages.title: Heal
pages.text:
$(l)Rune Sequence:$()
$(9)$(l) 20 Self CheckHealth - Self Heal$()

$(l)Effect:$()Heals your health up to 20 points.

$(l)Knowledge Points:$()
·$(9)CheckHealth$() pops entity, pushes its current health.
·$(9)-$() subtraction: 20 - current health = amount to heal.
·$(9)Heal$() pops entity and value, consumes mana to restore health. There are two $(9)Self$() on the stack — the second is the target entity for $(9)Heal$().

pages.title: Heal Related Rune Pages
pages.text: These are the runes used in this spell

pages.title: Flash Step
pages.text:
$(l)Rune Sequence:$()
$(9)$(l)Self VisionDirection 5 * Self Teleport$()

$(l)Effect:$()Instantly moves 5 blocks in your line of sight direction. Useful for crossing canyons.

$(l)Knowledge Points:$()
·$(9)VisionDirection$() pops entity, pushes the direction it's looking (unit vector).
·$(9)*$() scalar multiplication: stretches direction vector to 5 blocks.
·$(9)Teleport$() pops coordinate and entity, consumes mana to teleport entity. Note there are two $(9)Self$() on the stack — one to get vision direction, one is the teleport target.

pages.title: Flash Step Related Rune Pages
pages.text: These are the runes used in this spell

pages.title: Mana Ball
pages.text:
$(l)Rune Sequence:$()
$(9)$(l)[ 2.0 Explode ] Self VisionCoordinate ManaBall$()

$(l)Effect:$()Launches a mana ball from eye position, creating an explosion with radius 2 upon impact with blocks or entities.

$(l)Knowledge Points:$()
·Square brackets $(9)[ ... ]$() package a group of runes into a $(l)RuneRegister$() — runes in the register won't execute immediately, but are stored as a "spell package".
·When a $(9)ManaBall$() projectile hits something, it opens a new spell stack, automatically pushes the hit coordinate (Vec3), then executes its stored runes.

pages.text: These are the runes used in this spell

$(l)Tips and Next Steps$()

·Check mana before casting — spells with real-world effects consume mana, nothing happens if insufficient.
·Use $(9)StackState$() to view stack data if something goes wrong — it's your best debugging tool.
·Try modifying spell logic — what happens if you change Flash Step's 5 to 10? What if you add water placement before explosion and block breaking after in Mana Ball?

$(l)Quick Reference for Common Parameter Types$()

You've encountered these data types across six spells. Let's summarize:

·$(9)Double$() — Numbers. Like $(9)5.0$(), $(9)20$(). Used for calculations, distances, heal amounts.
·$(9)Vec3$() — Coordinates or vectors. Like vision coordinate, foot coordinate, vision direction. Consists of three numbers (x, y, z).
·$(9)Entity$() — Entities. $(9)Self$() pushes the player entity.
·$(9)Boolean$() — Boolean values, only $(2)true$() and $(4)false$(). Used in condition nodes next chapter.
·$(9)String$() — Strings. Wrapped in quotes, like $(9)"0"$(), mainly used for variable names.
·$(9)Object$() — Any type.

Understanding these types makes it easier to understand what inputs each rune needs and what outputs it produces when browsing the rune dictionary.
